title: Gonioscopy
what: The doctor places a special lens on your eye to look at the area where fluid drains out of the eye.
why: For glaucoma or suspected glaucoma, and before laser treatment for glaucoma.
duration: usually 5 to 15 minutes; the doctor tells you the result right away

prepare.title: Contacts
prepare.text: If you wear contact lenses, they will be taken out before the exam. Bring your case.

prepare.title: Getting there
prepare.text: Your vision may be a little hazy for a while. Plan your trip home.

steps: The eye is numbed with drops
You rest your chin on a stand
The doctor gently places a lens with gel on your eye
You are asked to look in different directions
The lens is removed, and the eye is rinsed if needed
feel: Usually no pain, just a touch
An urge to blink. The doctor will help hold the eyelid
after: Do not rub your eye while the numbing drops are working
Mild haziness and redness usually pass quickly
red_flags: Severe pain or worse vision after the exam: see a doctor

faq.a: Usually not. The eye is numbed with drops.

faq.q: How is this different from a regular exam?
faq.a: A regular exam does not show the drainage angle. That needs a special lens.

reminders.text: Eye exam in 2 hours. If you wear contacts, bring your case.
